summary: Robustness iteration 3 (final deferred slice), sprint 2026-W26: multi-device sessions (2b) + Redis rate-limit (3a). #25 CVE remediation already merged. Option A: sessions stay in PostgreSQL, Redis only for rate-limit buckets (Caffeine default). Waves continue the numbering (1-6 used). Wave 7 lands the token-model foundation (the breaking @OneToOne -> @ManyToOne rewrite + V6); Wave 8 runs the session endpoints (#48, depends on #47) in parallel with the Redis abstraction refactor (#49, independent files); Wave 9 adds the Redis-backed store (#50, depends on #49).

waves.label: Wave 7 — Multi-device foundation
waves.blurb: Token-model rewrite: RefreshToken @ManyToOne + session_id + device metadata, per-login row, per-session reuse detection, migration V6. Breaking change; everything else builds on it.

waves.label: Wave 8 — Session endpoints + Redis abstraction (parallel)
waves.blurb: #48 (list/revoke session endpoints — depends on #47, touches RefreshTokenService/controller) and #49 (RateLimitStore abstraction + Caffeine default — independent, touches rate-limit code). Different files, run concurrently.

waves.label: Wave 9 — Redis-backed store
waves.blurb: Profile-activated Redis-backed rate-limit store (bucket4j-redis). Depends on Wave 8's #49 abstraction.
